chunks: Say: "Just think: If God destroys me and those with me, or is benevolent to us, who will then protect the unbelievers from a painful doom?"
ai.seo_question: Who will protect the disbelievers from God's painful punishment if He wills?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah (Al-Malik) by questioning the efficacy of polytheist intercessors, emphasizing that divine decree is independent of human or idolatrous intervention. It serves as a reminder that whether God chooses to punish or show mercy, the ultimate authority rests solely with Him, rendering all other claims of protection futile.
